summary: Rebuild game dialogs from the panel_building kit (prototype)
author: client
body:
Goal (user, 2026-11-24): "Using this set of sheets, can you reconstruct some of the dialogs in the game such as the character dialog, chat history etc..."

Prototype only, in `.claude/scratch/panel_kit/`. Kit sheet: `working/sprite_work/panel_building.png` (read only).

Steps:
1. Slice the kit into named parts by alpha bounding boxes -> `panel_kit.json` + `parts/<name>.png` + labelled contact sheet.
2. Composer `compose.py`: panel of any size from (style, width, height, background, parts placed): background tile, border and corners per style, optional title divider, inner frames, buttons.
3. Reconstruct the character dialog and chat history dialog at in-game size and layout (plus one more if quick).
4. `<dialog>_compare.png` (original left, reconstruction right, same scale) plus each reconstruction at 1x and 2x, reviewed by eye.

Done when: the slice JSON, the composer and the compare images for the character dialog and chat history exist, and they have been reviewed by eye. No game code or staged art changes.

**Status, 2026-11-24:** The user approved the kit ("It looks significantly better - ship it") and chose to draw it in the client now. Shipping the kit and the client plan are under way, so this moves out of user_review.

comments.author: client
comments.body:
Prototype built in `.claude/scratch/panel_kit/` (scratch only; no game code or staged art touched).

- `compose.py`: `compose(size, background, border_style, corner_style, inner)` in the user's order (size -> background inset 1 px -> border -> corners -> inner placements); `recon/character_steps.png` shows each step.

Over to the user to judge the look by eye: frames and layout are close. The gaps are the warm title wash, the bevelled slot rings, the 74x20 text-button art and fainter flourishes.

comments.author: client
comments.body:
Follow-up (user: "This bitmap glyph decor needs to be semi-transparent, maybe additive blended?"):

- `compose.py`: decor parts take `blend` = `normal` (alpha * `opacity`) or `additive` (dst + src * alpha * opacity, clamped), through `blend_onto()`. Titles pass `ornament_blend`.
- Measured with `ornament_blend.py` against the original "Name & Status" knots (cached `originals/character.png`). Over two boxes round the flourishes it compares peak = mean of the brightest 15% of pixels, lift = peak minus the box median, and MAE:
  - original: peak (223,199,155), lift (91,84,65)
  - old opaque cream: peak (217,204,173), lift (78,86,81), MAE 26.4, score 36.9
  - additive cream 0.5: lift (101,96,81), score 40.0 (0.6 and 0.7 overshoot further)
  - alpha cream 0.6: lift (45,50,47), score 56.4 (too faint)
  - **additive warm (196,176,126) 0.5: peak (228,198,149), lift (87,78,55), MAE 25.1, score 31.7, the best**
- The default for flourishes is now additive 0.5 with the warm tint (`ORNAMENT_BLEND`, `ORNAMENT_WARM`). The dark wave flourishes (chat history, system menu) stay normal alpha, because additive can only brighten.
- `probe/ornament_strip_4x.png` shows original / old / additive warm 0.5 / alpha 0.6. `recon/character_compare.png` is regenerated and reviewed.

comments.author: client
comments.body:
Follow-up on the user's gap answers (2026-11-24):

1. Edge strip ("Can you show me what you mean?"): `recon/rim_compare.png` is a 6x zoom of the left edge with three panels:
   - original: 5 px rim + 3 px shadow;
   - now: the 9 px wood bar squeezed to 6 px, + 3 px shadow;
   - the raw 9 px kit bar.
   The gap: the kit has no thin rim strip, so a 5 px bronze strip (horizontal and vertical) would replace the squeeze.
2. Scrollbar ("Can use the square 2px bevel grove"): `scrollbar` is now a reusable placement. It is a sunken groove 9-sliced from the bevel square (any length; params `track_w`, `groove_darken`, `thumb`, `pos`). Chat history uses it at rect (340,28,15,121), track 6 px, thumb at the bottom (y 134 against the original's 133). The original's groove is narrower (about 3 px) and sits at the thumb's left edge; `track_w` can match that.
3. Flourish colour ("I want them to be able to be colored during runtime"): the flourishes stay black masks in the kit (verified: `divider_knot` holds only (0,0,0)). Tint, opacity, blend, emboss, mirror and scale are placement parameters, documented in `_part`. In the client, `DrawParams` tint is an additive offset (-255..+255), and black + offset = the tint colour:
   - normal = `tinted_alpha(r, g, b, opacity)`;
   - additive = `BlendMode::AdditiveOffset` (`additive_tinted`) with the offset pre-scaled by opacity. How that path weights alpha is unverified.
   - `additive_colored` multiplies, so it would keep black glyphs black; do not use it.
4. Ring size: left as is, per the user.
5. Text buttons: improvised ones kept until the user's 74x20 art arrives.

Regenerated all compares and reviewed them.

comments.author: client
comments.body:

**Button kit (`working/sprite_work/button_panel.png`).** 14 parts added to `panel_kit.json` with a `sheet` field:

comments.author: client
comments.body:
The user's Photoshop title recipe, button face textures v2, and faux-bold labels.

**Red titles (`text_fx.render_ps_title`, `ps_measure.py`, `ps_title.py`, `recon/ps_title.png`).** Scored on "Character Info." and "System Menu"; lower is better.
- Drop shadow: distance 1 at 120 degrees, opacity 75 %, hard, knocked out by the glyph. #241a18 at a rounded (1,1) offset is best (13.12); subpixel (0.5,0.87) scores 13.56 and (0,1) 14.49.
- The original's highlight sits 1 px up-left, outside the strokes; 97 % of the System Menu's brightest glyph pixels are on the upper-left edge. An overlay inside the glyph (edge cutout, top gradient, top half, full) does not improve on the shadow alone. The mask that works is the overlay text drawn 1 px up-left, outside the base glyph.
- Vivid Light, pink (255,190,170), 35 %: 11.53.
- **Additive, (120,85,75), 35 %: 11.38, now the default title stack.** The old emboss scores 11.11.
- Runtime: 3 draws per title.
  1. shadow at (+1,+1), normal blend, #241a18 at 0.75;
  2. highlight at (-1,-1), additive, (120,85,75) at 0.35;
  3. base fill on top.
  Drawing the fill last gives both the shadow knockout and the outside-only mask, so no clip rect, gradient alpha or mask texture is needed. Vivid Light would need a shader or a load-time bake, so it is not recommended.
  Unverified: whether the client's text renderer accepts an additive blend per draw (sprites do, via `DrawParams`). If it does not, bake each title once at load.

**Button kit v2.** The sheet is now 351x196.
- `btn_face_normal` and `btn_face_hover` are now 51x51 diagonal-grain textures at (240,2) and (292,2), tiled, never stretched. The old 6x6 swatches were removed.
- The frame, caps and cards are pixel-identical to before.
- Normal face colour is now close: (84,72,54) against (91,73,53). Hover is still darker: (124,58,25) against (146,87,40).
- Mean MAE went from 22.17 to 23.22 with the new faces, because textured faces with a different grain phase score worse than flat ones. By eye they are clearly closer.

**Small labels: faux-bold Wine Tahoma**, the glyph run drawn twice with the second copy +0.5 px in x; advance and tracking unchanged (`faux_bold.py`).
- Normal MAE: 24.38 regular, 24.97 at +1 px, **24.23 at +0.5 px**.
- Hover MAE: 24.09 regular, 24.10 at +1 px, **23.54 at +0.5 px**.
- Width ratio 1.02.
- It is now the default; 2 draws per label. If the client cannot position glyphs at a fractional x, use +1 px.
- Mean button MAE with it: 22.99.

Regenerated and reviewed: `buttons_compare.png`, `character_compare.png`, `sys_menu_compare.png`, `chat_history_compare.png`.

comments.body:
Faux-bold for all label text (user: "Name and status need to be bolded as well - same with the other label text"). Script: `bold_labels.py`; sheet: `probe/labels_bold.png`.

**Headings** (Tahoma 13 px with emboss), scored over both headings:

| Variant | MAE | Score | Draws |
|---|---|---|---|
| Regular (before) | 22.84 | 25.87 | 3 |
| Faux-bold +0.5, all passes | **22.71** | 28.72 | 6 |
| Faux-bold +0.5, fill only | 23.07 | 29.00 | 4 |
| Faux-bold +1, all passes | 25.56 | 28.68 | 6 |
| Faux-bold +1, fill only | 25.82 | 28.78 | 4 |

- Pick: **+0.5, all passes**. It has the lowest MAE of every variant and matches the original's weight at 4x. Its composite score is higher only through the fill and halo terms, because the half-pixel blend softens the core colour. +1 reads too heavy.
- Faux-bold on all passes beats fill only in both offsets.

**Field labels** (14 labels, dark ink; Level ... EK.Count, Str. ... Chr.):

| Variant | MAE | Score | Draws |
|---|---|---|---|
| Regular, 13 px (before) | 13.18 | 18.58 | 1 |
| **Faux-bold +0.5, 13 px** | **13.05** | 18.61 | 2 |
| Faux-bold +1, 12 px | 13.61 | 19.05 | 2 |

- Pick: **+0.5**. It is the closest weight by eye; the scores are equal within 0.03 and its MAE is lower.

**Draw counts:** headings 6 per string, field labels 2, small button labels 2 (unchanged). Red titles (3) and value text (1) stay as they were.

The system menu and chat history reconstructions have no label text: titles and chat lines only, and the chat lines are value text. Regenerated and reviewed all three compares.

The reconstruction used cream 11 px with a shadow, which is wrong. Values are now Tahoma 12 in (25,25,25) at the client's exact x ranges and y values, the same size as the labels. The name line uses `UIDarkRed` (58,0,0) at x 24-252, y 52; the status line uses (25,25,25) at x 0-275, y 69.

comments.author: client
comments.body:
Wide-button label font identification (user: "The font for the larger buttons is off - I presume wrong font ... could you do some comparisons?"). Research and mock-ups only, in `.claude/scratch/panel_kit/fonts_id/`; Windows fonts read only, nothing downloaded.

**Original** (normal-state wide buttons in `dialogtext_sprite_1.png`: Start, Create New Character, Delete Character, Change Password, Log Out):
- cap height 9-11 px (median 10);
- x-height 5-7 px, which depends on the threshold because the glyph edges are soft;
- thin, high-contrast strokes with wedge serifs and a binocular "g";
- word gaps a steady **8 px** (Times' space at this size is about 4.5 px);
- a dark (+1,+1) shadow.

**Candidates:** every installed serif and display face (Times New Roman, Georgia, Palatino Linotype, Cambria, Constantia, Sylfaen, Sitka, Gabriola, Copperplate Gothic, Clarendon), plus shipped Liberation Serif and Wine Tahoma; regular, bold and faux-bold each.
- Book Antiqua, Garamond, Century, Bookman, Baskerville, Perpetua and Trajan are not installed.
- Size fitted to cap height; letter spacing fitted to the word widths.
- Score = 100 x (1 - shape correlation) + word-width error %. Correlation is on blurred ink, with each word aligned on its own original word box.
- Raw pixel overlap and the x-height / weight features were tried and dropped: on 1 px strokes and soft edges they did not separate the fonts (the sans Tahoma scored mid-pack).

**Top 5:**
1. Liberation Serif faux-bold 14 px, track +0.5: corr 0.815, word error 2.7 %, score **21.2**
2. Liberation Serif regular 14 px: 0.792, 3.3 %, 24.1
3. Liberation Serif bold 14 px: 0.774, 2.5 %, 25.1
4. Times New Roman regular 14 px: 0.771, 2.6 %, 25.5
5. Constantia faux-bold 14 px: 0.773, 3.3 %, 26.0

Gabriola, Copperplate and Wine Tahoma are clearly wrong by eye.

**Conclusion:** the wide labels are Times New Roman (TTF, 14 px), which the shipped Liberation Serif reproduces metrically, so no new font is needed. Confidence: high for the family, from letterforms and word widths within about 3 %; moderate for the exact weight and effect. What looks "off" in the current rebuild is:
- word spacing about 4.5 px against the original's 8;
- the dark (+1,+1) shadow is missing;
- the weight is slightly light; the original sits between regular and faux-bold.

Recommended mock-up (bottom row of the sheet): Liberation Serif 14, track +0.5, 8 px word gap, shadow (+1,+1) at 0.6; faux-bold +0.5 like the other labels is worth trying.

Not a bitmap font: `dialogtext_sprite_1` holds whole pre-rendered buttons, not a glyph atlas. A direct check against the client sprite fonts (font1 / font2 / sprfonts) was not possible, because `build/pak_extracted/` is missing; unverified, but those are small pixel fonts with different letterforms.

Sheet: `fonts_id/font_compare2.png` (original + top 5 + recommended, 1x and 3x). Ranking: `fonts_id/ranking2.txt`; first pass `ranking.txt` / `font_compare.png`.

comments.author: client
comments.body:
Wide-button labels, weight vs drop shadow (user: "I like the bolder look - but maybe it's also because it has a drop shadow as the others?"). Script: `fonts_id/weight_vs_shadow.py`; sheet: `fonts_id/weight_vs_shadow.png`, plus a 4x strip `fonts_id/logout_5rows_4x.png`.

Liberation Serif 14, track +0.5, 8 px word gap, on the kit button face; scored against the five original wide labels. Ink coverage is the share of label pixels with L > 150; the original's is 0.070.

| Variant | corr | Word error | Coverage | font_id2 score | Combined |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regular, no shadow | 0.742 | 5.5 % | 0.078 (+11 %) | 31.3 | 42.5 |
| **Regular + shadow 60 %** | 0.735 | 5.5 % | 0.073 (+4 %) | 31.9 | **36.4** |
| Faux-bold +0.5, no shadow | 0.723 | 4.0 % | 0.105 (+50 %) | 31.7 | 81.4 |
| Faux-bold +0.5 + shadow 60 % | 0.717 | 4.0 % | 0.089 (+28 %) | 32.4 | 60.2 |

- Shape scores are within 1.1 points of each other, so darkness decides: **regular + shadow is closest**. Faux-bold puts 28-50 % more ink on the face than the original.
- So the bolder look is the shadow and contrast, not a heavier stroke. At 4x the original's strokes are as thin as regular; it reads bolder because its fill is brighter (about (247-255, 234-247, 214-222) against our (239,228,210)) and its shadow shows harder on a darker, noisier face.
- Next step, not done: regular + shadow with a brighter fill around (250,240,218) and a stronger shadow (0.75-0.8).

The button rebuild is unchanged.

comments.author: client
comments.body:
Wide-button labels, "bold under" stack (user: "Try it with a slightly darker bold under then the drop shadow as well"). Script: `fonts_id/bold_under.py`; sheets: `fonts_id/bold_under.png` (1x and 4x) and `fonts_id/logout_best2_4x.png`.

Stack, bottom to top: (+1,+1) shadow (24,16,8) of the faux-bold run; faux-bold +0.5 copy at fill x k; regular fill (250,240,218) on top. Liberation Serif 14, track +0.5, 8 px word gap, on the kit button face. Original ink coverage 0.070.

| Under-layer | Shadow | corr | Coverage | Score | Combined |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| x0.85 | 60 % | 0.719 | 0.114 (+63 %) | 32.1 | 94.9 |
| x0.85 | 80 % | 0.717 | 0.113 (+61 %) | 32.3 | 93.4 |
| x0.75 | 60 % | 0.716 | 0.104 (+49 %) | 32.5 | 81.7 |
| x0.75 | 80 % | 0.714 | 0.102 (+46 %) | 32.7 | 78.6 |
| x0.65 | 60 % | 0.712 | 0.098 (+40 %) | 32.9 | 72.6 |
| **x0.65** | **80 %** | 0.710 | 0.097 (+39 %) | 33.0 | **72.0** |

Word error 4.1 % for all.

- **Best: under x0.65 + shadow 80 %**, with 60 % as a near-tie runner-up. Darker under-layers are always better.
- None beats the earlier regular + shadow 60 % (combined 36.4). They all carry 39-63 % more bright ink than the original.
- By eye, at 4x, x0.65 / 80 % has the heavier, shadowed look the user likes, but its strokes are visibly thicker than the original's thin ones. The original's boldness comes from contrast, not stroke width.
- Caveat on the metric: the coverage threshold is L > 150, and an x0.65 under-layer (about L 157) still counts as ink. An under-layer at x0.55 or darker would read as a dark edge rather than extra weight; it is the obvious next step.
- Draw count per word run: shadow 2 (faux-bold) + under 2 + fill 1 = **5**. All are plain `draw_text` calls with `TextStyle` colour / alpha at x offsets; no shader, no additive. A shadow from the regular run would make it 4.
- The button rebuild is unchanged.

Button panel v4 (user: "I modified the button panel again as well"). Snapshot of the previous parts: `snapshot_btn_v3/`. Diffed piece by piece; the sheet is still 295x196.

- `btn_face_normal`, 25x25 at (241,2): repainted. Mean (87,72,50) -> (80,61,32), darker and warmer; std 17.8 -> 22.0.
- `btn_face_hover`: **moved** from (267,2) to (241,29), directly under the normal face, and repainted. Mean (124,58,25) -> (128,69,32). The old spot is now empty.
- Unchanged, pixel-identical: frame (8 pieces), caps (2), cards (2). Nothing else added or removed.
- Re-sliced (62 parts; `slice.py` points at the new hover position). The `wide_button_label` recipe is kept in `panel_kit.json`.

Re-score (all 9 buttons x 2 states):
- Mean MAE **22.68 -> 21.66**; every hover button improved (for example Ok 18.0 -> 14.4, Start 19.3 -> 15.6). Normal buttons are about 1-2 worse.
- Normal face colour: (84,69,47) -> **(77,58,29)** against the original (91,73,53). It is now slightly too dark and too yellow; the blue channel is about 24 low.
- Hover face colour: (122,56,23) -> **(128,69,32)** against the original (146,87,40). Closer, still about 18 darker.
- Tile repeat: the face is still 25x25, so the wide-button repeat is unchanged (exact every 25 px, against the original's -0.05 to 0.21). The tiling method is left alone, because the texture is not large enough to remove the repeat; that would need a tile at least as wide as the face (about 170 px).

Regenerated and reviewed `recon/buttons_compare.png`.

comments.body:
Shipped (user: "It looks significantly better - ship it"; "The dialog kit can be shipped now too").

- Tool `tools/panel_kit/`:
  - `build_panel_kit.py` slices `working/sprite_work/panel_building.png` and `button_panel.png` and packs the atlas.
  - `compose.py` is the reference composer, drawing from the staged kit only.
  - `text_fx.py` holds the multi-pass text.
  - The reconstruction and scoring scripts stay in scratch.
- Kit `staged/client/sprites/panelkit/`:
  - `panel_kit.png` (1024x565, 83 pieces) and `panel_kit.json`, the full dialog kit:
    - backgrounds; wood_light and wood_dark borders; stone, rivet and gold corners;
    - bevel box (inset and raised), rules, ring_bevel and the 23 small buttons;
    - 3 flourishes, the scrollbar groove and thumb, and the button frame, faces and caps.
  - The JSON adds the recipes: backgrounds, border/corner styles, inner, nine_slice, flourish tints, button states, and text recipes as draw lists.
  - Brightening, per-channel multiply, alpha gain, the 6 px borders and the 26 px ring are baked, because the renderer draws with alpha only.
  - The character-select cards are not shipped (the plates stay).
- Byte-for-byte proof:
  - `--check` reports identical (exit 0).
  - Two fresh builds into scratch match the staged copy (`cmp`); sha256 png ed8d41bf..., json c6c7ac0b....
- Fidelity: the staged-kit composer matches the approved scratch composer. Small and wide hover buttons are pixel-identical (MAE 0); the framed panel is at MAE 0.017, max 1.
- Spec: `.claude/design/plans/panel-kit-runtime.md` (10.2 KB), with 8 steps, the last dropping the old sprites; it includes a usage census per game_dialogs sprite.
- Client work: task HH-0059, blocked by HH-0060 to HH-0067.
